chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, compiler of this book — may God have mercy on him — said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Abbas ibn Umar al-Fuqaymi, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he
said to the atheist who had asked him, 'From where do you prove the prophets and messengers?' He said:

'When we established that we have a Creator, a Maker, Exalted above us and above all that He created, and that this Maker was Wise and Transcendent — so that His creatures cannot behold Him nor touch Him, and He cannot deal with them directly nor they with Him, and He cannot argue with them directly nor they with Him — it is established that He has ambassadors among His creation who convey on His behalf to His creation and His servants, guiding them toward their interests and benefits and that by which they endure, while its neglect means their destruction.

Thus it is established that there are those who command and forbid on behalf of the Wise, the All-knowing, among His creation, who convey from Him — Majestic and Mighty — and they are the prophets (peace be upon them) and His chosen elites from His creation: wise ones disciplined with wisdom, sent with it, yet without sharing in anything of the conditions of the people despite their commonality with them in creation and composition, supported by the Wise, the All-knowing with wisdom.

Then this has been established in every era and time through what the messengers and prophets have brought of proofs and demonstrations, so that God's earth shall not be devoid of a divine authority who possesses knowledge indicating the truthfulness of his claim and the validity of his justice.'

key_terms.الحكيم العليم: The Wise, the All-knowing — divine attributes emphasizing that prophets are sent by an omniscient God
key_terms.الزنديق: Zindiq — an atheist or freethinker who denies divine revelation
key_terms.الصفوة: The chosen elite — the special status of prophets as God's selected representatives
key_terms.حجة: Hujja — divine proof or authority; in Shia theology, always present on earth
key_terms.سفراء: Ambassadors/emissaries — the prophets acting as divine intermediaries

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq prove the necessity of prophets and messengers?
ai.summary: This hadith records a rational theological argument by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in response to an atheist who questioned the existence of prophets. The Imam argues that since the Creator is transcendent and cannot directly communicate with creation, He necessarily sends ambassadors — the prophets — who are specially chosen, wise, and supported by divine wisdom, to guide humanity in every age. The argument is rooted in the principle that a transcendent God would need intermediaries to guide human beings, and that the continuity of prophets and messengers throughout history confirms this theological necessity.
